input: Research Peloton (onepeloton.com) for a hedge fund

risks.claim: Subscriber contraction can overwhelm price-led monetization: at September 30, 2026, paid Connected Fitness subscriptions were 2.475 million, down 9% year over year; paid App subscriptions were 0.487 million, down 10%. Current Q2 guidance anticipates further Connected Fitness contraction.

Headline profitability is not a clean recurring run rate: management described approximately $25 million of nonrecurring Q1 FY2027 EBITDA benefits; full-year guidance was unchanged despite the quarter’s beat. The quarter should not be annualized without accounting for those benefits and seasonality.

Holiday execution matters: on November 5 management said Q2 sales are heavily back-weighted to Black Friday, Cyber Monday and winter holidays; guidance balances refreshed-Tread optimism against demand uncertainty. Commercial trials are not yet proof of durable consumer or institutional growth.

Financing execution remains open: the November 9 launch left coupon and other note terms to pricing, and notes closing is not conditioned on the new revolver or old-loan repayment. Intended refinancing benefits should not be booked as completed.

Litigation overhang persists: the November 5 10-Q reports dismissal with prejudice of the seat-post-related securities case on March 31, 2026, an appeal notice April 30 and plaintiffs’ appeal brief August 14. No dated appellate decision in the next six months was verified.

catalysts.claim: Week of November 9, 2026: pricing of the proposed $600 million debut high-yield bond is a near-term catalyst. November 9 reporting said sale was due that week; timing is indicative, not a confirmed closing date. Final pricing and completion were not verified as of November 10.

December 8, 2026, 11:00 a.m. ET: virtual annual meeting; agenda includes election of one Class I director, auditor ratification and advisory say-on-pay frequency. This is a scheduled governance event, not a disclosed change-of-control vote.

Spring 2027: Tread Flex is scheduled to expand outside North America; Australia is described as autumn 2027. The September 22 announcement provides a seasonal window, not a day-specific launch; part of that window could fall after May 10.

event_driven.claim: November 9 refinancing launch: proposed $600 million senior secured notes due 2032 plus a $200 million five-year revolver; proceeds and cash are intended to retire the existing term loan. This is a financing proposal, not a completed transaction as established by the announcement.

As of November 9, possible residual-proceeds uses include Class A repurchases and acquisitions, but the release does not announce an authorized buyback amount, tender offer or acquisition. Do not treat the permitted-use language as an announced capital-return or M&A program.

output.research_view: As of November 10, 2026, the immediate catalyst is refinancing execution, but stronger cash generation is not yet evidence that subscriber erosion has stopped ([refinancing announcement](https://investor.onepeloton.com/news-releases/news-release-details/peloton-interactive-inc-announces-launch-global-refinancing-0/); [Q1 results](https://investor.onepeloton.com/news-releases/news-release-details/peloton-announces-q1-fy2027-financial-results/)). The key operating test is whether the refreshed treadmill range and commercial channel can offset the fading pricing tailwind without sacrificing cash flow; unchanged annual guidance and nonrecurring quarterly benefits argue against extrapolating the headline earnings beat ([earnings call](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/11/05/peloton-pton-q1-2027-earnings-call-transcript/)).

credit_signals.claim: As of September 30, 2026: cash and equivalents $1,342.2 million; outstanding term-loan principal $977.5 million and existing revolver undrawn. These balances precede the subsequent voluntary paydown and proposed refinancing.

October 9, 2026: voluntary $280 million term-loan repayment reduced that loan’s principal to $697.5 million. November 5 disclosure put post-paydown total gross principal debt at $1.048 billion, down 32% from December 31, 2025.

Contractual maturities disclosed as of September 30, before the proposed refinancing: existing term loan and revolver mature May 30, 2029; $350 million of 5.50% convertible notes mature December 1, 2029. The proposed secured notes would mature in 2032, subject to completion.

Existing revolver covenants disclosed November 5 require $250 million total liquidity and $1.2 billion trailing-four-quarter subscription revenue only when revolving loans are outstanding; the undrawn facility did not require financial-covenant testing. These are existing, not final replacement-facility terms.

November 9 rating coverage: S&P assigned BB- issuer credit with stable outlook and BB to the proposed secured debt; Moody’s assigned Ba3 to proposed notes and SGL-1 liquidity. Proposed ratings do not establish that the financing has closed.

missing_fields: catalysts.dated court or regulatory decisions through 2027-05-10

alternative_signals.claim: As reported November 5 for Q1 FY2027: commercial business revenue grew 13% year over year. Management described trials and advanced conversations with gym and hospitality operators; these are pipeline indications, not disclosed signed contracts or quantified backlog.

As of the November 5 results release, ten additional U.S. microstores had opened since the beginning of Q1, bringing the fleet to 19. This is an owned-channel expansion signal rather than independent evidence of sell-through.

September 22 product announcement set North American availability from October 1, 2026: Tread Flex starting at US$2,195, Tread Vision US$3,495. October 1 channel reporting observed delivery windows of October 11–18 in some U.S. ZIP codes; this is a dated availability check, not a November inventory measurement.

January 30, 2026: Reuters reported an 11% workforce reduction, primarily affecting engineering. Latest official status in the November 5 filing says the 2024 and 2025 restructuring plans were substantially completed by June 30, 2026; no material further charges were expected under the 2025 plan.

As of November 5, management attributed Q1 revenue growth to prior-year pricing changes and said that tailwind begins to lap midway through Q2 FY2027. New-product adoption must therefore offset weaker pricing comparisons; no new subscription price increase is asserted here.

results_vs_guidance.claim: Q1 FY2027, ended September 30, 2026: revenue $559.2 million, up 2% year over year; company reported revenue $4 million above guidance midpoint. Gross margin 61.3% beat 57% guidance, partly from nonrecurring benefits; paid Connected Fitness subscriptions 2.475 million were at guidance’s upper end.

Q1 FY2027 adjusted EBITDA was $167.8 million versus the company’s August 6 guidance of $135–145 million; GAAP net income was $96.2 million and free cash flow $143.4 million for the quarter ended September 30. Original revenue guidance was $545–565 million and subscription guidance 2.455–2.475 million.

Q1 FY2027 consensus comparison, reported November 5: diluted EPS $0.19 versus analyst estimate $0.11; revenue $559.2 million versus $554.55 million consensus. These are the contemporaneous figures reported by Investing.com; its guidance paragraph mislabels annual revenue as quarterly and is not used.

Current Q2 FY2027 guidance as of November 5: revenue $625–650 million, gross margin approximately 50%, adjusted EBITDA $85–100 million and ending paid Connected Fitness subscriptions 2.425–2.445 million. Revenue midpoint implies a 3% year-over-year decline.

Current FY2027 guidance as of November 5, unchanged: revenue $2.30–2.40 billion, gross margin approximately 54%, adjusted EBITDA $475–525 million and free cash flow at least $350 million; revenue midpoint implies a 4% year-over-year decline.

insider_and_ownership.claim: October 20, 2026: Chief Accounting Officer Saqib Baig sold 10,000 Class A shares at $5.45, leaving 257,729 directly held shares. The Form 4 says the sale followed a Rule 10b5-1 plan adopted September 2, 2025; it is a pre-planned sale, not an insider purchase.

October 15, 2026: COO Charles Peter Kirol vested 56,510 RSUs; 28,849 shares at $5.33 were withheld for tax liability, leaving 197,334 directly held common shares. The filing footnote identifies withholding, not an open-market bearish sale.

October 23 proxy ownership table, based on October 14, 2026 shares outstanding and cited holder filings: BlackRock 58,215,193 Class A shares (13.5% of Class A), Vanguard 24,549,783 (5.7%), DNB 22,685,343 (5.3%), Nantahala 21,547,895 (5.0%) and T. Rowe Price 21,760,678 (5.1%). These are proxy-reported holdings, not real-time positions.

October 23 proxy identifies underlying Schedule 13G/A filing dates of June 4, 2026 for BlackRock, July 31 for Vanguard and August 11 for DNB. Ownership is sourced to the opened proxy; direct amendment-level ownership changes were not independently verified.

As of June 30, 2026, DME Capital had exited Peloton, selling 10,113,940 shares during Q2, according to August 24 reporting on its 13F. This is secondary-source evidence of a historical exit, not proof of its position on November 10.
